public_rationale: OpenAI and DeepSeek announced further cuts after the post. September 2026 reporting documents another competitive episode and connects it to increasingly comparable alternatives. That meets the early-resolution rule for price wars continuing. Support depends on reading 'moat' as differentiation among model offerings and accepting credible reporting of competitive pressure as evidence of a contributing cause.
limitations: The causal evidence is reporting and analyst assessment, not a controlled economic study.
Some reductions accompanied replacement models, so they are not all cuts to identical products.
This does not establish that all prices fell or that competition must continue indefinitely.
The separate profits statement is outside this assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Because OpenAI's moat keeps shrinking, price wars among AI model providers will continue.

statement.excerpt: That said, OpenAI’s moat keeps diminishing, so price wars will continue and profits will continue to be elusive for everyone except Nvidia.

our_interpretation: The assessed proposition concerns price competition, not the separate statement about profits.
The plain reading is that increasingly competitive alternatives to OpenAI will drive further rounds of price competition among model providers.
I interpret moat here as differentiation from competing model offerings. Marcus supplies no measure of its size.
The word 'so' asserts a causal explanation, rather than making an explicit if-then forecast.
A documented renewed episode can establish that price wars continued; the wording does not require prices to decline forever or every provider to cut every price.
criteria.support_condition: After publication, multiple model providers make further competitive price reductions, with credible evidence linking that competition to increasingly comparable rival offerings.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence establishes that the asserted renewed competitive episode did not occur or that the claimed erosion of differentiation did not drive it. A temporary pause or an isolated price increase would not suffice.

evidence.explanation: Confirms a post-publication reduction on an existing OpenAI model. It does not independently establish the reason for the cut.

Confirms further reductions by a competing provider when introducing a replacement model. The announcement also attributes lower costs to efficiency gains, so this item alone cannot establish Marcus's causal explanation.

evidence.locator: Article standfirst; supporting detail in 'The pressure from open source'
evidence.explanation: Reports a renewed competitive pricing episode involving OpenAI and rival providers, explicitly connecting pressure to alternatives offering comparable performance. This supplies the competitive explanation absent from the earlier price announcements; it relies partly on analyst assessments.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The reported launch forms part of a renewed competitive pricing episode across providers, explicitly linked to comparable rival offerings. Together with the earlier provider disclosures, it establishes continuation after the post.
